title: He built India's first digital computer. Decades later, he built the machine that counts India's votes.

sources.text: Electronics Corporation of India Limited - Official history
Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India - A.S. Rao profile

caption:
He built India's first digital computer. Decades later, he built the machine that counts India's votes.

Rao founded the Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) in 1967, tasked with building India's electronics and computing capability from near zero, at a time when computers were imported, foreign-built machines.

Under Rao, ECIL didn't just assemble foreign designs - it designed and manufactured computers domestically through the 1970s, giving India its own computing base at a time almost no developing country had one.

A company founded to prove India could build its own computers went on to build the machines that record and verify how a billion-plus people vote - a direct line from one founder's mandate to the mechanics of the world's largest democracy.
